\chapter{Introduction}
\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:introduction}}\label{\detokenize{01_introduction::doc}}

\section{Purpose and scope}
\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:purpose-and-scope}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Copernicus Programme, established by the European Union, is a framework for Earth Observation and Monitoring, designed to support environmental protection, civil protection, and civil security efforts. At the heart of this programme is the Copernicus Space Component (CSC), which comprises the Sentinel missions. These missions are integral to providing essential data across various thematic domains, thereby facilitating informed decision\sphinxhyphen{}making and policy development.

\sphinxAtStartPar
One of the new advancements within this framework is the Copernicus Radar Observing System for Europe \textendash{} L\sphinxhyphen{}Band (ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L). This initiative is aimed at enhancing existing capabilities by introducing L\sphinxhyphen{}band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data. The L\sphinxhyphen{}band SAR is set to complement the C\sphinxhyphen{}band radar data provided by Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}1, thus addressing specific observational needs within environmental and maritime surveillance.


\section{Cal/Val context}
\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:cal-val-context}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Quality Assessment (QA) is required for remote sensing and Earth Observation (EO) instruments in order to produce reliable measurements and ensure accuracy. Quality of products are commonly assessed through a Calibration and Validation process (Cal/Val). Consequently, the development of the prototype and operational ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L Ocean products processors (L2O\sphinxhyphen{}GPP and L2O\sphinxhyphen{}IPF respectively) must be followed by the validation of products. A validation strategy is meant to be planned prior the calibration and validation activities. The required strategy shall cover different stages of the processor and different phases of ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L mission, from pre\sphinxhyphen{}launch (phase D) to exploitation (phase E2). The strategy shall include methodologies, datasets, performance and uncertainty metrics.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L instrument will operate in scanning synthetic aperture radar (ScanSAR) mode. The system will support Dual\sphinxhyphen{}Pol, Quad\sphinxhyphen{}Pol and Wave modes. The Cal/Val strategy is also meant to cover all modes and polarizations. ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L will not be the first SAR system functioning within L\sphinxhyphen{}band. ALOS, ALOS\sphinxhyphen{}2, ALOS\sphinxhyphen{}4, SAOCOM and NiSAR are, or have been, operating in L\sphinxhyphen{}band too. However, there are differences between those systems and the ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L system, e.g. incidence angle, range bandwith, swath width, among others. Furthermore, ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L incorporates the use of a new technique, the Scan\sphinxhyphen{}On\sphinxhyphen{}Receive (SCORE) technique with Multiple Azimuth Phase Centers (MAPS). The different instrument design will impose differences in the retrievals at low level which are meant to influence the inversion into L2 products.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Regarding the development of a retrieval algorithm but also Cal/Val activities, instrument differences between ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L and previous SAR L\sphinxhyphen{}band instruments impose a challenge; the need of producing and validating ocean products from ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L scenes during the pre\sphinxhyphen{}launch phase. The lack of real ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L data will be mitigated by the use of similar acquisitions by the above\sphinxhyphen{}mentioned systems; although this introduces a non\sphinxhyphen{}negligible degree of uncertainty. For Cal/Val purposes, simulated ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L scenes will be produced. The achievable accuracy of simulated ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L will also be analysed during the In\sphinxhyphen{}Orbit\sphinxhyphen{}Commissioning (IOC) phase, E1. Once real ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L data is available, the outputs from the L2O\sphinxhyphen{}IPF processor will need to be validated again, with the possibility to encounter a need for a readjustment of the processor or introduction of supplementary calibration steps.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A tool for assessing the quality of the ocean products is vital. The Cal/Val tool, L2O\sphinxhyphen{}QC, is meant to be developed in parallel to the development of the ocean processors, L2O\sphinxhyphen{}GPP and L2O\sphinxhyphen{}IPF. The L2O\sphinxhyphen{}QC software is required to be able to ingest datasets of different nature; ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L acquisitions, reference datasets (either in\sphinxhyphen{}situ or remote), and auxiliary data. The goal is to collocate the different datasets in order to undertake the quality assessment, where the accuracy and reliability of the ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L L2 ocean products will be determined and ensured. The underlying objective is to provide users with a set of performance and uncertainty metrics necessary for a deep understanding of the products and posterior correct usage and application.


\section{L2 product scope}
\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:l2-product-scope}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The L2 products to validate are already listed in the objectives of L2O\sphinxhyphen{}GPP and L2O\sphinxhyphen{}IPF: Ocean Surface Vector Stress (OSVS), Sea State, and line\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}sight (LoS) surface currents. Within each of the three thematic products, the following L2 variables are meant to be produced and therefore validated:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
OSVS:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Wind vector

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Wind stress

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hub height wind speed

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sea state:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Total significant wave height

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mean period wind\sphinxhyphen{}sea

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
First moment wave period

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Second moment wave period

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Wave height swell dominant system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Wave height swell secondary system

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Significant wave height wind\sphinxhyphen{}sea

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mean period wind\sphinxhyphen{}sea

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Wave direction

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Wave directional energy spectrum

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LoS currents:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LoS wave Doppler

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LoS surface current component

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\section{Cal/Val objectives and performance}
\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:cal-val-objectives-and-performance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The key objectives of the Calibration and Validation (Cal/Val) phase include ensuring that all L2 geophysical products meet internationally recognized standards, such as SI traceability, and align with QA4EO principles to guarantee high data quality. Cal/Val aims to validate the accuracy, precision, and stability of L2 products using independent datasets, such as Fiducial Reference Measurements (FRM), and cross\sphinxhyphen{}sensor harmonization. A critical focus is on quantifying and documenting uncertainty propagation from instrument measurements to retrievals while ensuring the retrieval algorithms are robust under diverse environmental conditions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To meet performance requirements, L2 products must achieve predefined thresholds in accuracy, precision, and stability, with uncertainties traceable and reliable across pixel and aggregate levels. Products must demonstrate consistency over full mission coverage, addressing global, regional, and temporal scales, and maintain defined operational latencies (e.g., near\sphinxhyphen{}real\sphinxhyphen{}time or reprocessed outputs). Validation activities use measurable metrics, including statistical bias, RMS error, and spatial\sphinxhyphen{}temporal coverage rates, to assess product quality systematically. Lastly, the outputs should be delivered in user\sphinxhyphen{}ready formats with comprehensive documentation while maintaining version control and data provenance.


\section{ATBD purpose}
\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:atbd-purpose}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The aim of the Calibration and Validation Algorithm Theoretical Basis Document (ATBD) is to provide a comprehensive and transparent description of the scientific principles, mathematical methods, and processing steps used to generate ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L L2 ocean products. It ensures that the algorithms are well\sphinxhyphen{}documented, reproducible, and traceable, facilitating a clear understanding of how measurements are transformed into geophysical quantities. The ATBD serves as a foundation for ensuring data quality, guiding calibration/validation efforts, and supporting user confidence in the satellite mission’s outputs.

\section{Definitions and conventions}
\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:definitions-and-conventions}}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Accuracy\index{Accuracy@\spxentry{Accuracy}|spxpagem}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:term-Accuracy}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The quality of being near to the true value. The source marks this
definition as requiring a reference.

\sphinxlineitem{Comparison\index{Comparison@\spxentry{Comparison}|spxpagem}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:term-Comparison}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Metrologists validate uncertainty analysis and confirm traceability
through comparisons. The Mutual Recognition Arrangement requires
regular, formal international comparisons to establish the degree of
equivalence between SI realisations and disseminations in different
countries.

\sphinxlineitem{Dataset\index{Dataset@\spxentry{Dataset}|spxpagem}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:term-Dataset}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A combination of data records, such as numerical values needed to analyse
and interpret a natural process, and the related information content.

\sphinxlineitem{Fiducial Reference Measurement\index{Fiducial Reference Measurement@\spxentry{Fiducial Reference Measurement}|spxpagem}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:term-Fiducial-Reference-Measurement}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A suite of independent, fully characterised, and traceable sub\sphinxhyphen{}orbital
measurements, relevant to space\sphinxhyphen{}based observations, following the
guidelines of the GEO/CEOS Quality Assurance Framework for Earth
Observation (QA4EO).

\sphinxlineitem{Fundamental Data Record\index{Fundamental Data Record@\spxentry{Fundamental Data Record}|spxpagem}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:term-Fundamental-Data-Record}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A record, of sufficient duration for its application, of
uncertainty\sphinxhyphen{}quantified sensor observations calibrated to physical units
and located in time and space, together with ancillary and lower\sphinxhyphen{}level
instrument data used to calibrate and locate the observations and to
estimate uncertainty ({\hyperref[\detokenize{04_uncertainty_analysis:ref-qa4eo1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Woolliams et al. 2025a}}}}}).

\sphinxlineitem{Interoperability\index{Interoperability@\spxentry{Interoperability}|spxpagem}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:term-Interoperability}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ability of data or tools from non\sphinxhyphen{}cooperating resources to integrate
or work together with minimal effort (\sphinxhref{https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18}{Wilkinson et al. (2016)}%
\begin{footnote}[2]\sphinxAtStartFootnote
\sphinxnolinkurl{https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18}
%
\end{footnote}).

\sphinxlineitem{Interoperable\index{Interoperable@\spxentry{Interoperable}|spxpagem}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:term-Interoperable}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Describes data or tools from non\sphinxhyphen{}cooperating resources that can integrate
or work together with minimal effort (\sphinxhref{https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18}{Wilkinson et al. (2016)}%
\begin{footnote}[3]\sphinxAtStartFootnote
\sphinxnolinkurl{https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18}
%
\end{footnote}).

\sphinxlineitem{Measurand\index{Measurand@\spxentry{Measurand}|spxpagem}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:term-Measurand}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The quantity intended to be measured, and the single output quantity from
a measurement model.

\sphinxlineitem{Metrology\index{Metrology@\spxentry{Metrology}|spxpagem}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:term-Metrology}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The science of measurement and its application
({\hyperref[\detokenize{04_uncertainty_analysis:ref-jcgmvim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{BIPM et al., n.d.\sphinxhyphen{}b}}}}}).

\sphinxlineitem{Thematic Data Product\index{Thematic Data Product@\spxentry{Thematic Data Product}|spxpagem}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:term-Thematic-Data-Product}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A record, of sufficient duration for its application, of
uncertainty\sphinxhyphen{}quantified retrieved values of a geophysical variable, along
with ancillary data used in retrieval and uncertainty estimation.

\sphinxlineitem{Traceability\index{Traceability@\spxentry{Traceability}|spxpagem}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:term-Traceability}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A property of a measurement relating its value to a stated metrological
reference through an unbroken chain of calibrations or comparisons, with
uncertainties evaluated and methodologies documented at each step.

\sphinxlineitem{Uncertainty analysis\index{Uncertainty analysis@\spxentry{Uncertainty analysis}|spxpagem}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{01_introduction:term-Uncertainty-analysis}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The review of uncertainty sources and their propagation through the
traceability chain, based on the suite of documents prepared by the JCGM
and known as the GUM.

\end{description}

\chapter{Processing model and data flow}
\label{\detokenize{02_processing_model:processing-model-and-data-flow}}\label{\detokenize{02_processing_model::doc}}

\section{Overview and top\sphinxhyphen{}down decomposition}
\label{\detokenize{02_processing_model:overview-and-top-down-decomposition}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The source describes the calibration and validation activities across the
ROSE\sphinxhyphen{}L mission phases. It does not provide a detailed processing\sphinxhyphen{}block
decomposition or an algorithm\sphinxhyphen{}level data\sphinxhyphen{}flow diagram.


\section{Pre\sphinxhyphen{}launch phase (D)}
\label{\detokenize{02_processing_model:pre-launch-phase-d}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
During the pre\sphinxhyphen{}launch phase (phase D), activities focus on preparing and
validating the L2 processing chain, ensuring readiness for on\sphinxhyphen{}orbit operations.
Key tasks include finalizing L2 requirements, algorithms, and performance
budgets. Simulators and proxy datasets are leveraged to validate retrieval
algorithms and uncertainty models. Pre\sphinxhyphen{}launch instrument characterization is
integrated into the processing chain to ensure retrievals are robust to on\sphinxhyphen{}orbit
conditions. A comprehensive Cal/Val Plan is developed, identifying validation
sites, protocols, data matchups, and metrics.


\section{Commissioning phase (IOC or E1)}
\label{\detokenize{02_processing_model:commissioning-phase-ioc-or-e1}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the commissioning phase (IOC or phase E1), the primary goal is to validate
L2 products using on\sphinxhyphen{}orbit data and release initial beta/provisional products
with documented performance. Early activities include confirming L1
performance, performing vicarious calibrations, and matching L2 products with
ground\sphinxhyphen{}based and airborne reference datasets (FRM sites, buoys, ship\sphinxhyphen{}based
campaigns, etc.). Algorithms are fine\sphinxhyphen{}tuned using real\sphinxhyphen{}time data, and initial
uncertainty models are validated. Early reprocessing cycles are conducted to
improve product stability, and performance against key metrics is assessed.
Products are released with quality summaries, and ongoing monitoring dashboards
are set up.


\section{Exploitation phase (E2)}
\label{\detokenize{02_processing_model:exploitation-phase-e2}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The exploitation phase (phase E2) ensures L2 products maintain accuracy,
precision, and stability over the mission lifecycle. Routine validation is
conducted using reference networks, continuous KPI monitoring, and periodic
reprocessing cycles for algorithm and calibration improvements. Traceability
to standards (QA4EO, FRM) and uncertainty validation is maintained, while
long\sphinxhyphen{}term drift corrections support stable time series. Community engagement,
user feedback, and updates to documentation (validation reports, product
guides) are prioritised. The goal is to achieve validated product maturity,
ensuring high\sphinxhyphen{}quality data for science and operational applications.


\section{End\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}end data flow}
\label{\detokenize{02_processing_model:end-to-end-data-flow}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
No end\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}end processing\sphinxhyphen{}flow diagram, processing\sphinxhyphen{}step mapping, or algorithm
identifiers are provided in the source LaTeX document.

\chapter{Reference datasets description}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:reference-datasets-description}}\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:sec-ref}}\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}}, reference data are used for both calibration and validation of SAR\sphinxhyphen{}derived geophysical parameters. The L2 calibration process is exclusively implemented through Numerical Weather Prediction Ocean Calibration (NOC), which is specifically applied to the wind vector under the OSVS thematic area. Validation is performed against multiple independent reference sources for all thematic areas. The following sections describe the reference datasets used for calibration and validation purposes.


\section{Ocean Surface Vector Stress}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:ocean-surface-vector-stress}}

\subsection{Wind vector}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:wind-vector}}

\subsubsection{C\sphinxhyphen{}band SAR}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:c-band-sar}}

\paragraph{Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}1 L2 OCN \sphinxhyphen{} OWI}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:sentinel-1-l2-ocn-owi}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Ocean Wind field (OWI) component of the Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}1 Level\sphinxhyphen{}2 Ocean (L2\_OCN) product, providing 10 m neutral wind speed and direction on a regular grid, derived from the Level\sphinxhyphen{}1 SAR backscatter using a CMOD5.N geophysical model function. The OWI component is available in Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}1 Interferometric Wide (IW), Extra Wide (EW), and Stripmap (SM) acquisition modes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In general, L1 and L2 Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}1 products are generated by the Instrument Processing Facility (IPF) and carry an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ipf\_version}} with them to distinguish between different processing versions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
land pixels are masked in the source product. The OWI product is typically delivered at an 1x1 km grid for all acquisition modes. The nominal swath widths are mode dependent with IW \(\sim 250\) km, EW \(\sim 400\) km, and SM \(\sim 80\) km.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The OWI product carries a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wind\_quality}} flag and an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inversion\_quality}} flag. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inversion\_quality}} is related to the inversion, which depends on the NRCS, incidence angle, azimuth look angle and ancillary wind speed and direction. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inversion\_quality}} flag indicates the consistency between SAR and ancillary winds. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wind\_quality}} flag is more general including both the inversion quality as well as the geophysical quality for the whole product.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{inversion\_quality}} flag has the following values:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0: high quality

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1: medium quality

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2: low quality

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wind\_quality}} flag has had several different classifications. Currently (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ipf\_version}} \(= 4.03\)) it ranges from 0 \textendash{} 4, where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0: no data

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1: bad

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2: suspect

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
3: acceptable

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
4: good.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the past (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ipf\_version}} \(<4.03\)), its range ran from 0 \textendash{} 3, where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0: high quality

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1: medium quality

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2: low quality

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
3: bad quality.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To avoid interpreting the wrong meaning, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wq\_flag\_meanings}} is read from the metadata before filtering.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only high/medium (acceptable/good) flags are accepted. In addition, data points are rejected when both flags are NaN.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
3 April 2014 \sphinxhyphen{} present with global coverage (6 days revisit rate).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (\sphinxurl{https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/}); OData catalogue/download API at \sphinxurl{https://catalogue.dataspace.copernicus.eu/odata/v1/Products}; free registration required.


\paragraph{RADARSAT\sphinxhyphen{}2 Wind}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:radarsat-2-wind}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
An independently\sphinxhyphen{}derived high\sphinxhyphen{}resolution sea surface wind speed product distributed by NOAA/NCEI, derived from RADARSAT\sphinxhyphen{}2 C\sphinxhyphen{}band SAR backscatter. Wind speed at 10m height is retrieved by inverting the CMOD4 geophysical model function.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
wind speed only (sub\sphinxhyphen{}kilometer pixel resolution). The accompanying direction field is the NWP\sphinxhyphen{}model direction used to resolve the CMOD4 180\(^\circ\) ambiguity, not an independently retrieved SAR direction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two distinct filename/metadata eras exist in the archive (pre\sphinxhyphen{} and post\sphinxhyphen{}2024).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Post\sphinxhyphen{}2024 RADARSAT\sphinxhyphen{}2 wind files carry \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pixel\_level\_quality\_flags}} parameter that can be used to mask land/ice/quality. A cell is deemed valid when this flag equals 5 (“valid wind in valid water region”). Pre\sphinxhyphen{}2024 files only contain a coarser mask/ice\sphinxhyphen{}mask combination, which is used as fallback \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mask==\sphinxhyphen{}1 \& icemask==1}}. All other cells are given \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NaN}} as value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
May 2014 \sphinxhyphen{} present (\(\sim 1\) month latency). The available data via NOAA is heavily centered around the polar regions with most occurrences near Alaska and the Bering strait as can be seen in Figure \hyperref[\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:fig-radarsat2-coverage}]{Fig.\@ \ref{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:fig-radarsat2-coverage}}}.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics[width=1.000\linewidth]{{radarsat2_global_coverage_density}.png}
\caption{Coverage of RADARSAT\sphinxhyphen{}2 high resolution sea surface winds via the NOAA/NCEI THREDDS archive. The center locations of all 32742 available RADARSAT\sphinxhyphen{}2 products from May 2014 \sphinxhyphen{} July 2026 have been plotted.}\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:fig-radarsat2-coverage}}\end{figure}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
NOAA NCEI THREDDS catalogue, \sphinxurl{https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/thredds-ocean/catalog/sar-winds/radarsat2/catalog.html} (public, no authentication); per\sphinxhyphen{}granule bounding boxes are available via THREDDS’ NCML metadata service, avoiding full\sphinxhyphen{}file downloads for non\sphinxhyphen{}overlapping scenes.


\subsubsection{Numerical Prediction Model}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:numerical-prediction-model}}

\paragraph{ERA5 Reanalysed wind}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:era5-reanalysed-wind}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
hourly, global 10 m wind field from ECMWF’s ERA5 atmospheric reanalysis, produced under the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) and distributed via the Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS). Used as an independent, model\sphinxhyphen{}based reference wind field, collocated via bilinear spatial and hyperbolic temporal interpolation rather than point/swath matching.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
global regular latitude/longitude grid at 0.25° spacing, hourly output. The 10 m zonal and meridional wind components (\(u_{10}\), \(v_{10}\)) are retrieved from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reanalysis\sphinxhyphen{}era5\sphinxhyphen{}single\sphinxhyphen{}levels}} dataset, together with a land\sphinxhyphen{}sea mask (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lsm}}); wind speed and direction are derived after interpolation to the query location.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
grid cells/query points with \(\mathrm{lsm} > 0.5\) (land) are excluded before collocation. ERA5 is documented and evaluated in (Hersbach et al. 2020); an independent characterisation of its 10 m wind field (Belmonte Rivas and Stoffelen 2019) reports mean wind biases of up to 0.5 m/s in the zonal and meridional components, stable over time (interannual variability \(\sim\)0.1 m/s), and roughly 20\% lower instantaneous RMS wind speed error than the preceding ERA\sphinxhyphen{}Interim reanalysis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
1940 \sphinxhyphen{} present with global coverage. A preliminary near\sphinxhyphen{}real\sphinxhyphen{}time extension (ERA5T, \(\sim\)5 day latency) is later superseded by the quality\sphinxhyphen{}controlled final release (\(\sim\)3 month latency).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
CDS dataset \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reanalysis\sphinxhyphen{}era5\sphinxhyphen{}single\sphinxhyphen{}levels}}, via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cdsapi}} Python client; requires free CDS registration, with the API key stored in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciitilde{}/.cdsapirc}}.


\subsubsection{In\sphinxhyphen{}Situ Observations}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:in-situ-observations}}

\paragraph{ECMWF MARS archive}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:ecmwf-mars-archive}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Buoy observations relayed onto the WMO Global Telecommunication System (GTS) and archived by ECMWF’s Meteorological Archival and Retrieval System (MARS), retrieved with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{obstype=181/182}} (BUFR moored and drifting buoys respectively). Relevant variables are near\sphinxhyphen{}surface wind speed (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WSPD}}) and direction (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WDIR}}). As default, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} validates against GTS. Copernicus Marine in\sphinxhyphen{}situ data (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:subpar-cmems-insitu}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Copernicus Marine}}}}}) can be used as alternative or a waterfall combining both: the waterfall downloads both sources for the full recipe bounding box and window, then at collocation\sphinxhyphen{}tree build time drops any Copernicus Marine station whose platform ID GTS already reported for that window, preferring GTS’s value wherever GTS itself reports.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
point observations at native platform sampling rate ranging from once every 3\sphinxhyphen{}hrs to every 6\sphinxhyphen{}minutes. Default collocation in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} uses the point vs layer scheme with aggregation windows of \(\pm\)30 min / 5 km default radii (user adjustable via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.yaml}} recipe file).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Individual GTS BUFR reports carry no per\sphinxhyphen{}observation quality flag, because GTS requires the data processing center that owns a buoy to run automatic real\sphinxhyphen{}time quality control before an observation is transmitted onto the GTS (Panel 2011). The mandated real\sphinxhyphen{}time checks include, among others:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Gross error checks against fixed physical limits. For wind, 0\textendash{}100 m/s (speed) and 0\textendash{}360\(^\circ\) (direction).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Climatological limit checks against operator\sphinxhyphen{} or International Comprehensive Ocean\sphinxhyphen{}Atmosphere Data Set (ICOADS)\sphinxhyphen{}supplied bounds for the platform’s location and season.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Land/sea test; any observations that appear on land are rejected.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Location sanity checks (rejecting \((0,0)\), \(\pm180^\circ\), \(\pm90^\circ\) sentinel coordinates; a drifting buoy’s position older than 48 hours, or a moored buoy’s position older than its own (re\sphinxhyphen{})deployment age).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Checksum/Cyclic Redundancy Checks (CRC) validation of the transmision link between platform, satellite, and ground station.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Duplicate/near\sphinxhyphen{}duplicate observation suppression, and cascading rejection when an associated depth level or compensating sensor itself fails QC.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the quality checks performed by the owners of the platforms before ingestion into the GTS database, there are delayed mdoe quality control guidelines in place. Principle meteorological and oceanographic centers, including ECMWF, compare buoy reports against NWP model analysis to check for erroneous or biased data, feeding corrections back to the platform operators (Panel 2011).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ECMWF MARS archive has archived data from 28\sphinxhyphen{}11\sphinxhyphen{}2016 \sphinxhyphen{} present.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
ECMWF MARS archive (\sphinxurl{https://www.ecmwf.int/en/forecasts/access-forecasts/access-archive-datasets}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{obstype=181/182}} (BUFR moored and drifting buoys), retrieved via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ecmwf\sphinxhyphen{}api\sphinxhyphen{}client}} Python package (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ecmwfapi.ECMWFService}}); credentials read from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciitilde{}/.ecmwfapirc}} (ECMWF’s standard Web API key file), obtained through an ECMWF Member/Co\sphinxhyphen{}operating\sphinxhyphen{}State\sphinxhyphen{}affiliated account. The request shape is day\sphinxhyphen{}based and global, meaning that each retrieval contains all wind, wave, and currents sections a given buoy reported for that day. Data is provided in daily BUFR files.


\paragraph{Copernicus Marine}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:copernicus-marine}}\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:subpar-cmems-insitu}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Dataset ID INSITU\_GLO\_PHYBGCWAV\_DISCRETE\_MYNRT\_013\_030, which contains in\sphinxhyphen{}situ observations. Relevant platforms reporting near\sphinxhyphen{}surface wind speed (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WSPD}}) and direction (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WDIR}}) are moored buoys, drifting buoys, ferryboxes, and tidal gauges.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
point observations at native platform sampling rate, which is typically hourly or every 10\sphinxhyphen{}minutes. Default collocation in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} uses point vs layer collocation. The aggregation windows, which are user adjustable via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.yaml}} file, utilize \(\pm\)30 min / 5 km aggregation radii.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Copernicus Marine in situ Thematic Assembly Centre (TAC) has no commitment to manage in situ meteorological observations. Reported quality flags are kept in the NetCDF files, with no additional quality control (Wehde et al. 2025). The QC flag ranges from 0 \textendash{} 9 (Copernicus In Situ Tac Data Management Team 2025):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0: No QC was performed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1: Good data

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2: Probably good data

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
3: Bad data although potentially correctable

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
4: Bad data

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
5: Value changed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
6: Value below detection/quantification

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
7: Nominal value (e.g. reported rather than observed value like instrument target depth)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
8: Interpolated value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
9: Missing value

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Due to the lack of additional quality control, buoy data from the ECMWF MARS archive is preferred.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Platform dependent, the Copernicus marine environment monitoring services (CMEMS) dataset provides both historical data per platform and recent data. Not all platforms have both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WSPD}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WDIR}} available. Geographical coverage in 2026 can be seen in Figure \hyperref[\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:fig-in-situ-wind-coverage}]{Fig.\@ \ref{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:fig-in-situ-wind-coverage}}}.

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics[width=1.000\linewidth]{{insitu_wind_global_coverage_2026-08-01_2026-08-15}.png}
\caption{Coverage of Copernicus Marine in\sphinxhyphen{}situ platforms that provided wind speed and direction during the first half of August 2026.}\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:fig-in-situ-wind-coverage}}\end{figure}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Copernicus Marine in\sphinxhyphen{}situ dataset (\sphinxurl{https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/INSITU\_GLO\_PHYBGCWAV\_DISCRETE\_MYNRT\_013\_030/}), download via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{copernicusmarine}} Python client (free registration).


\subsubsection{Scatterometers}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:scatterometers}}

\paragraph{ASCAT}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:ascat}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
L2 product of 10 m neutral wind speed and direction wind\sphinxhyphen{}vector cells (WVCs) retrieved from C\sphinxhyphen{}band backscatter measured by the Advanced Scatterometer (ASCAT) aboard MetOp\sphinxhyphen{}B and MetOp\sphinxhyphen{}C, processed and distributed by EUMETSAT’s Ocean and Sea Ice Satellite Application Facility (OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF) as product OSI\sphinxhyphen{}104 (“ASCAT Wind Product”).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
dual fan\sphinxhyphen{}beam swath geometry, two \(\sim\)550 km wide swaths either side of the sub\sphinxhyphen{}satellite track separated by a \(\sim\)360 km nadir gap; wind\sphinxhyphen{}vector cells are provided on a regular along\sphinxhyphen{}/across\sphinxhyphen{}track grid at 12.5 km spacing. Data are distributed as 2\sphinxhyphen{}D swath NetCDF files and flattened to a point\sphinxhyphen{}geometry representation before collocation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
each WVC carries a bitmask \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wvc\_quality\_flag}}; cells for which any of the following bits are set are rejected before collocation:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
some portion of the WVC is over land

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
some portion of the WVC is over ice

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
wind inversion not successful

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
not enough good \(\sigma_0\) measurements for wind retrieval

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
distance to the geophysical model function (GMF) too large

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Furthermore, the OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF ASCAT (Metop\sphinxhyphen{}B/C) global 25 km and coastal 12.5 km wind products have been validated using buoys and triple collocation (Verspeek et al. 2019), showing wind quality well within the OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF product requirements (\(<2\) m/s wind component standard deviation, \(<0.5\) m/s speed bias). Against buoys, speed bias of 0.10/0.08 m/s and u\sphinxhyphen{}/v\sphinxhyphen{}component standard deviations of 1.62/1.90 (Metop\sphinxhyphen{}B) and 1.59/1.89 m/s (Metop\sphinxhyphen{}C) were found at 12.5 km. Triple collocation gives scatterometer\sphinxhyphen{}perspective errors of 0.62/0.78 (Metop\sphinxhyphen{}B) and 0.67/0.78 m/s (Metop\sphinxhyphen{}C) in the u\sphinxhyphen{}/v\sphinxhyphen{}components at 12.5 km (Verspeek et al. 2019).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
MetOp\sphinxhyphen{}B (launched 2012) and MetOp\sphinxhyphen{}C (launched 2018) provide continuous global coverage.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
EUMETSAT Data Store, collection \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EO:EUM:DAT:METOP:OSI\sphinxhyphen{}104}}, via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eumdac}} Python client (free registration).


\paragraph{HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B/HY\sphinxhyphen{}2C}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:hy-2b-hy-2c}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
10 m wind speed and direction wind\sphinxhyphen{}vector cells retrieved from Ku\sphinxhyphen{}band backscatter measured by the scatterometers aboard Haiyang\sphinxhyphen{}2B (HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B) and Haiyang\sphinxhyphen{}2C (HY\sphinxhyphen{}2C) ocean satellites (CNSA/NSOAS), reprocessed into the same OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF wind\sphinxhyphen{}product format/flag conventions as ASCAT and redistributed via KNMI’s OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF wind FTP server.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B/HY\sphinxhyphen{}2C carry a Ku\sphinxhyphen{}band, wide\sphinxhyphen{}swath (\(\sim\)1700 km) pencil\sphinxhyphen{}beam scatterometer; wind\sphinxhyphen{}vector cells are provided at 25 km spacing/resolution.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wvc\_quality\_flag}} bitmask and rejection criteria as ASCAT (see above) apply, capable of flagging rainy WVCs. Furthermore, the OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B and HY\sphinxhyphen{}2C wind products have been validated using buoys and triple collocation (Verhoef et al. 2024), showing wind quality well within the OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF product requirements (\(<2\) m/s wind component standard deviation , \(<0.5\) m/s speed bias). Against buoys, speed bias of \sphinxhyphen{}0.09/\sphinxhyphen{}0.06 m/s and u\sphinxhyphen{}/v\sphinxhyphen{}component standard deviations of 1.68/1.64 m/s (HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B) and 1.75/1.76 m/s (HY\sphinxhyphen{}2C) were found. Triple collocation gives scatterometer\sphinxhyphen{}perspective errors of 0.59/0.39 (HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B) and 0.81/0.65 (HY\sphinxhyphen{}2C) in the u\sphinxhyphen{}/v\sphinxhyphen{}components (Verhoef et al. 2024).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B (launched 2018) and HY\sphinxhyphen{}2C (launched 2020) are operational and provide global coverage. However, currently only the most recent 3 days with a \(\sim2.5\) hour latency (rolling window) are automatically available in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}}. Data is available in both NetCDF and BUFR format.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF wind FTP server (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ftppro.knmi.nl}}), directories \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/scat/netcdf/hy2b}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/scat/netcdf/hy2c}}; registered OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF FTP credentials required. Only a 3\sphinxhyphen{}day rolling window is available.


\paragraph{Oceansat\sphinxhyphen{}3}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:oceansat-3}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
10 m sea surface wind speed and direction wind\sphinxhyphen{}vector cells retrieved from the Ku\sphinxhyphen{}band scatterometer aboard ISRO’s Oceansat\sphinxhyphen{}3 (EOS\sphinxhyphen{}06), reprocessed into the OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF wind\sphinxhyphen{}product format and redistributed via the same KNMI FTP server as HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B/HY\sphinxhyphen{}2C.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
same 25 km wind\sphinxhyphen{}vector\sphinxhyphen{}cell spacing and Ku\sphinxhyphen{}band, wide\sphinxhyphen{}swath pencil\sphinxhyphen{}beam geometry as HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B/HY\sphinxhyphen{}2C.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wvc\_quality\_flag}}\sphinxhyphen{}based rejection criteria as ASCAT/HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B/HY\sphinxhyphen{}2C. Furthermore, the OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF Oceansat\sphinxhyphen{}3 wind products have been validated using buoys and triple collocation (Verhoef et al. 2024), showing wind quality well within the OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF product requirements (\(<2\) m/s wind component standard deviation , \(<0.5\) m/s speed bias). Against buoys, speed bias of \sphinxhyphen{}0.16 m/s and u/v component standard deviations of 1.72/1.68 m/s were found (Verhoef et al. 2024). Triple collocation gives scatterometer\sphinxhyphen{}perspective errors of 0.68/0.54 in the u\sphinxhyphen{}/v\sphinxhyphen{}components (Verhoef et al. 2024).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Oceansat\sphinxhyphen{}3 launched November 2022 and provides global coverage. Similarly to HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B and HY\sphinxhyphen{}2C, currently only the most recent 3 days with a \(\sim2.5\) hour latency (rolling window) are available in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}}. Data is available in both NetCDF and BUFR format.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF wind FTP server (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ftppro.knmi.nl}}), directory \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/scat/netcdf/oceansat3}}; registered OSI\sphinxhyphen{}SAF FTP credentials required. Only a 3\sphinxhyphen{}day rolling window is available.


\subsubsection{Radiometers}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:radiometers}}

\paragraph{RSS microwave radiometers (AMSR2, GMI, SSMIS, WindSat)}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:rss-microwave-radiometers-amsr2-gmi-ssmis-windsat}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Level\sphinxhyphen{}3 (L3), daily, global 10 m ocean surface wind speed products retrieved from passive microwave brightness temperatures, produced by Remote Sensing Systems (RSS) for six sensors: AMSR2 (GCOM\sphinxhyphen{}W1, JAXA), GMI (GPM, NASA/JAXA), SSMIS (DMSP F16/F17/F18; NASA), and WindSat (Coriolis, US Navy). WindSat additionally provides wind direction via its polarimetric channels; the other sensors are wind\sphinxhyphen{}speed\sphinxhyphen{}only.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
each sensor is distributed as a daily file already resampled to a common global 0.25° grid, with two passes (ascending/descending) per file and a per\sphinxhyphen{}cell measurement time. AMSR2 is published in NetCDF; GMI, SSMIS, and WindSat are distributed as gzipped RSS binary bytemaps. Wind speed is retrieved from a shared physical emissivity model (Meissner and Wentz 2012); cells under rain, land, or ice are already set to fill/NaN by RSS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
no per\sphinxhyphen{}cell quality bitmask is exposed; instead, invalid retrievals (rain\sphinxhyphen{}, land\sphinxhyphen{}, or ice\sphinxhyphen{}contaminated cells) are already flagged as fill values by RSS and dropped on read. Under rain\sphinxhyphen{}free conditions, RSS radiometer wind speed retrievals have a reported accuracy of \(\sim\)1 m/s RMS against buoys (Meissner and Wentz 2012); WindSat wind direction retrieval accuracy (all\sphinxhyphen{}weather algorithm) ranges from \(\sim\)10° in light rain to \(\sim\)30° at the onset of heavy rain, with wind speed accuracy degrading from 2 m/s to 4 m/s over the same range (Meissner and Wentz 2009).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
AMSR2 (2012\sphinxhyphen{}present), GMI (2014\sphinxhyphen{}present), SSMIS F16 (2003\sphinxhyphen{}present), SSMIS F17 (2006\sphinxhyphen{}present), SSMIS F18 (2009\sphinxhyphen{}present), WindSat (2003\sphinxhyphen{}present); all provide global coverage via twice\sphinxhyphen{}daily (ascending/descending) overpasses.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Remote Sensing Systems public HTTPS archive (\sphinxurl{https://data.remss.com/}), no account required; AMSR2 as NetCDF, GMI/SSMIS/WindSat as gzipped binary bytemaps.

\paragraph{WAVEWATCH III}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:wavewatch-iii}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
NOAA/NCEP’s operational third\sphinxhyphen{}generation spectral wave model WAVEWATCH III (WW3), currently run as GFS\sphinxhyphen{}Wave and one\sphinxhyphen{}way coupled into the Global Forecast System (GFS) v16 via the NEMS/NUOPC coupling infrastructure. Used as an independent, physics\sphinxhyphen{}based wave\sphinxhyphen{}model reference, collocated via bilinear spatial and hyperbolic temporal interpolation. The current operational code version (v6.07, released by the WAVEWATCH III Development Group in 2019 as the model’s first open\sphinxhyphen{}development GitHub release), run with the ST4 source\sphinxhyphen{}term physics package (wind input and dissipation) of (Ardhuin et al. 2010).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
global 0.16° regular latitude/longitude grid, with finer nested regional grids covering the Atlantic, East Pacific, and West Coast (all 0.16°), the Arctic (9 km), and the Southern Ocean (0.25°); the finest grid whose bounding box fully contains the query region is selected, falling back to the global grid otherwise. GFS\sphinxhyphen{}Wave initialises four times daily (00/06/12/18 UTC); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} reconstructs an hourly series from each cycle’s short\sphinxhyphen{}range forecast leads. The model parameter significant height of combined wind waves and swell (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HTSGW}}) is used as validation against SAR significant wave height.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
no per\sphinxhyphen{}cell quality flag is provided in the GRIB2 output; land points are implicitly absent from the ocean model grid. The ST4 physics package used by the current operational configuration has been shown to outperform the older ST2 (Tolman\textendash{}Chalikov) package used by earlier WAVEWATCH III code versions across most sea states, with the largest improvement in storm/extreme conditions add citation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
From March 2021 (GFSv16/v6.07 implementation) \textendash{} present, global coverage, published four times daily with hourly archived output between cycles.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
NOAA Open Data on AWS, bucket \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{noaa\sphinxhyphen{}gfs\sphinxhyphen{}bdp\sphinxhyphen{}pds}} (\sphinxurl{https://noaa-gfs-bdp-pds.s3.amazonaws.com}), public and unsigned HTTPS/S3 access, no authentication required; GRIB2 format, parsed via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eccodes}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cfgrib}} libraries.


\subsubsection{C\sphinxhyphen{}band SAR}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:c-band-sar-1}}\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:id1}}

\paragraph{Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}1 L2 OCN \sphinxhyphen{} OSW}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:sentinel-1-l2-ocn-osw}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The OSW component of the S1 L2\_OCN product provides partition\sphinxhyphen{}based wave parameters, including a significant wave height \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hs}} for each identified wave partition, as well as a vignette\sphinxhyphen{}level total significant wave height {[}m{]}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{total\_hs}}, and its standard deviation, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{total\_hs\_standard\_deviation}}. The partition quantities describe individual wave systems resolved in the OSW wave spectrum, whereas \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{total\_hs}} represents an integrated sea\sphinxhyphen{}state estimate for the vignette. From IPF 3.9.0 onward the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{total\_hs}} implementation is based on a variant of the deep\sphinxhyphen{}learning approach of Quach et al. (Quach et al. 2021). The OSW component is generated for Stripmap (SM) and Wave (WV) acquisition modes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
in WV mode, acquisitions consist of isolated \(\sim 20 \times 20\) km vignettes roughly 200 km apart along the orbit track, rather than a continuous swath, with one wave spectrum estimate per vignette.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In SM mode, the  80×170 km swath itself is tiled into a grid of  20×20 km OSW cells without gaps in between, unlike WV’s sparse sampling. Each OSW cell contains its own independent wave spectrum/partition estimate.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The OSW product carries a total \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{quality\_flag}} (0 \textendash{} 3), a per\sphinxhyphen{}partition \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{partition\_quality\_flag}} (0 \textendash{} 4), a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{land\_flag}}, a per\sphinxhyphen{}partition \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wave\_direction\_partition\_ambiguity}} flag, and a scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{snr}}, where for the total quality flag:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0: high quality

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1: medium quality

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2: low quality

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
3: bad quality

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
and, similarly but more finely graded, for the per\sphinxhyphen{}partition quality flag:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0: very good

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1: good

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2: medium

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
3: low

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
4: poor

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wave\_direction\_partition\_ambiguity}} flag (0 or 1) indicates, per partition, whether the retrieved wave propagation direction is uniquely resolved or subject to the inherent \(180^\circ\) ambiguity of SAR\sphinxhyphen{}derived wave direction; as it concerns direction rather than the wave height itself, it is not used for filtering \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{total\_hs}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Data points are rejected when the total quality flag (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{quality\_flag}}) is \(\geq 2\), or when the land flag is set. However, the total quality flag currently only contains fill values as it does not seem to be populated by the operational processor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
3 April 2014 \textendash{} present. Unlike OWI’s continuous\sphinxhyphen{}swath coverage, WV mode acquires sparse, isolated vignettes along the orbit track rather than continuous global coverage. Note that the total significant wave height, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{total\_hs}}, is only available since 2022 (Johnsen et al. 2022). In addition, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{total\_hs}} was unavailable for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ipf\_version}} 3.8.0, after which it was reactivated from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ipf\_version}} 3.9.0 onwards. The significant wave height partition, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hs}}, was not affected by these changes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (\sphinxurl{https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/}); OData catalogue/download API at \sphinxurl{https://catalogue.dataspace.copernicus.eu/odata/v1/Products}; free registration required.

\paragraph{Copernicus Marine}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:subpar-cmems-insitu-waves}}\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:id4}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Dataset ID INSITU\_GLO\_PHYBGCWAV\_DISCRETE\_MYNRT\_013\_030, which contains in\sphinxhyphen{}situ observations. Relevant platforms reporting significant wave height are buoys, moorings, and tidal gauges.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
point observations at native platform sampling rate; default collocation, which is user adjustable, is \(\pm\)30 min / 5 km aggregation radius.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Copernicus Marine in situ TAC aggregates operational oceanography data and metadata from multiple providers, ingested with varying confidence depending on the data source (Copernicus In Situ Tac Data Management Team 2025). Bad flags are preserved and an additional quality control is performed that may result in a QC flag degradation (never an upgrade). For waves, this additional quality control procedure applies 7 different tests to wave parameters as described in the Copernicus Marine In Situ TAC quality control procedure (2025) (Copernicus In Situ Tac Data Management Team 2025).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The quality flag ranges from 0 \textendash{} 9:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
0: No QC was performed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
1: Good data

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
2: Probably good data

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
3: Bad data although potentially correctable

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
4: Bad data

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
5: Value changed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
6: Value below detection/quantification

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
7: Nominal value (e.g. reported rather than observed value like instrument target depth)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
8: Interpolated value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
9: Missing value

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Accepted QC flag codes are \(\{1,2,5,7,8\}\). A significant part of the data available on Copernicus Marine In situ lacks a QC and is thus dropped before validation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Accuracy of the measurements provided by Copernicus Marine is sensor dependent, but all sensors have an uncertainty of maximum 1\% or 0.1 m (Wehde et al. 2025). The estimated accuracy due to statistical variability is \(< 5\)\% for SWH (Wehde et al. 2025).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Platform dependent, some platforms provide a long history. Not all platforms have both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WSPD}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{WDIR}} available. Geographical coverage can be seen in Figure \hyperref[\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:fig-in-situ-waves-coverage}]{Fig.\@ \ref{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:fig-in-situ-waves-coverage}}} for the first half of August 2026. Moorings and tidal gauges have fixed locations, while the buoys drift.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Copernicus Marine in\sphinxhyphen{}situ dataset (\sphinxurl{https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/INSITU\_GLO\_PHYBGCWAV\_DISCRETE\_MYNRT\_013\_030/}), download via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{copernicusmarine}} Python client (free registration).

\subsubsection{Altimeters}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:altimeters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
SWH altimeter observations are divided into a reprocessed version that currently has 1 Hz altimeter data from 03\sphinxhyphen{}08\sphinxhyphen{}1991 \sphinxhyphen{} 31\sphinxhyphen{}12\sphinxhyphen{}2023 (Charles and Ollivier, n.d.) and a near\sphinxhyphen{}real time (NRT) version that contains 1 Hz sampled altimeter data from 28\sphinxhyphen{}12\sphinxhyphen{}2023 \sphinxhyphen{} present and 5 Hz sampled altimeter data from 09\sphinxhyphen{}03\sphinxhyphen{}2026 \sphinxhyphen{} present (Philip et al., n.d.).


\paragraph{Global Ocean L3 Significant Wave Height from Reprocessed Satellite Measurements}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:global-ocean-l3-significant-wave-height-from-reprocessed-satellite-measurements}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This reprocessed dataset provides significant wave height data derived from satellite altimeter data including the Topex, ERS\sphinxhyphen{}1/2, Jason\sphinxhyphen{}1/2/3, Envisat, Saral/AltiKa, Cryosat\sphinxhyphen{}2, and Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}3A/3B/6A missions as well as altimeter L3 V4 data from the ESA Climate Change Initiative (CCI) Sea State project. The along\sphinxhyphen{}track measurements from the different missions are combined into a single daily file, thus resulting in a unified dataset combining all available missions. The dataset includes distance to coast, sea floor depth below mean sea level, sea surface wave significant height (regular, adjusted, denoised) and its uncertainty (Charles and Ollivier, n.d.).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The 1 Hz sampling corresponds to an along track resolution of 7 km, resulting in a default aggregation window of 7 km and 180 min in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} tool. Jason\sphinxhyphen{}2 serves as a calibration anchor and CCIv4 improves cross\sphinxhyphen{}calibration across all missions. The denoised SWH is used as validation dataset. Denoising means cross\sphinxhyphen{}mission bias correction and Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) denoising following Quilfen and Chapron (2019) (Quilfen and Chapron 2021).

\sphinxAtStartPar
For Topex, Jason\sphinxhyphen{}1/2/3, and Sentinel 6\sphinxhyphen{}A, the coverage is maximum 66°S/66°N in latitude; for SARAL/AltiKa 81.5°S/81.5 °N; for Cryosat\sphinxhyphen{}2 88°S/88°N; for ERS\sphinxhyphen{}1/2, Envisat, and Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}3A/3B 90°S/90°N (Charles and Ollivier, n.d.).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data Quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A strict QC filter is applied before creating of the dataset, only allowing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{swh\_quality\_level}} \(= 3\) (good data) to be included. No QC filtering is needed in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} tool and no quality flags themselves are not provided in the dataset.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
03\sphinxhyphen{}08\sphinxhyphen{}1991 \sphinxhyphen{} 31\sphinxhyphen{}12\sphinxhyphen{}2023; 1 Hz sampling frequency.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Copernicus Marine satellite altimetry dataset (\sphinxurl{https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/WAVE\_GLO\_PHY\_SWH\_L3\_MY\_014\_005/}), download via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{copernicusmarine}} Python client (free registration).


\paragraph{Global Ocean L3 Significant Wave Height from NRT Satellite Measurements}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:global-ocean-l3-significant-wave-height-from-nrt-satellite-measurements}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The product consists of an inter\sphinxhyphen{}calibrated, denoised multi\sphinxhyphen{}mission altimeter\sphinxhyphen{}derived along\sphinxhyphen{}track SWH dataset. It combines 1 Hz sampling data from CFOSAT, CryoSat\sphinxhyphen{}2, HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B/2C, Jason\sphinxhyphen{}3, Saral/AltiKa, Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}3A/3B/6A, and SWOT nadir producing sea surface wave significant height (filtered and unfiltered) as well as sea surface wind speed. The 5 Hz sampling contains data from CryoSat\sphinxhyphen{}2, Jason\sphinxhyphen{}3, Saral/AltiKa, and Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}3A/3B/6A and produces sea surface wave significant height (filtered and unfiltered).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The data from the different missions are homogenized with respect to a reference mission (Jason\sphinxhyphen{}3 until April 2022, Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}6A afterwards). The 1 Hz sampling corresponds to an along track resolution of 7 km, resulting in a default aggregation window of 7 km and 180 min. The 5 Hz sampling has an along track resolution of 1.4 km, resulting in a default aggregation window of 1.4 km and 180 min in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} tool.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For Jason\sphinxhyphen{}3, Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}6A and Hai Yang\sphinxhyphen{}2C, the coverage is maximum 66°S/66°N in latitude; for Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}3A, Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}3B and AltiKa, 81.5°S/81.5°N; for Cryosat\sphinxhyphen{}2, 88°S/88°N; for HaiYang\sphinxhyphen{}2B, 81°S/81°N; for CFOSAT, 83°S/83°N and for SWOT, 78°S/78°N. Note that for Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}3A and B, the altimeter wave measurements are deduced from both SAR measurements.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data Quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Prior to inclusion in the dataset, data is selected based on a combination of various criteria such as quality flags and parameter thresholds, including surface flag, presence of ice, sigma0 (mission dependent), SWH (min: 0 m; max: 30 m), wind speed (min: 0 m/s; max: 30 m/s), sigma0 standard deviation (min: 0 dB; max 3 dB), shoreline distance (\(\geq 0\)) (Philip et al., n.d.). Only data points passing these criteria are included in the dataset. No QC filtering is needed in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} tool and no quality flags themselves are not provided in the dataset.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
1 Hz sampling rate: late 2023 \sphinxhyphen{} present; note that the NRT 1 Hz dataset is used from 01\sphinxhyphen{}01\sphinxhyphen{}2024 onward to replace the reprocessed one that ends 31\sphinxhyphen{}12\sphinxhyphen{}2013. 5 Hz sampling rate: 09\sphinxhyphen{}03\sphinxhyphen{}2026 \sphinxhyphen{} present. Availability delay is 3 hours for all satellites other than HY\sphinxhyphen{}2B/2C, which are provided with a delay of 7 hours.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Copernicus Marine satellite altimetry dataset (\sphinxurl{https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/WAVE\_GLO\_PHY\_SWH\_L3\_NRT\_014\_001/}), download via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{copernicusmarine}} Python client (free registration).

\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:nwp-1}}\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:id6}}

\paragraph{HYCOM}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:hycom}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The HYbrid Coordinate Ocean Model (HYCOM) is a data\sphinxhyphen{}assimilative, eddy\sphinxhyphen{}resolving global ocean general circulation model producing three\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional fields of ocean state (Chassignet et al. 2009). Its vertical coordinate is hybrid, blending isopycnal (density\sphinxhyphen{}following) layers in the stratified open ocean, terrain\sphinxhyphen{}following layers in shallow coastal regions, and fixed pressure\sphinxhyphen{}level coordinates in the surface mixed layer and/or unstratified open seas. This toolbox uses HYCOM’s surface\sphinxhyphen{}level (\(z=0\)) horizontal current velocity, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{water\_u}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{water\_v}}, drawn from two HYCOM configurations: Global Ocean Forecasting System (GOFS) 3.1 Analysis (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GLBy0.08/expt\_93.0}}; 04\sphinxhyphen{}12\sphinxhyphen{}2018 \sphinxhyphen{} 10\sphinxhyphen{}08\sphinxhyphen{}2024) (Metzger et al. 2017), and its higher\sphinxhyphen{}resolution successor ESPC\sphinxhyphen{}D\sphinxhyphen{}V02 (10\sphinxhyphen{}08\sphinxhyphen{}2024 onwards), the ocean component of the Navy’s Earth System Prediction Capability (Navy\sphinxhyphen{}ESPC) (Barton et al. 2021). The eastward/northward current vector at each grid cell is projected onto the local SAR LoS (radial) direction for direct comparison against radial surface\sphinxhyphen{}velocity measurements, using the same heading\sphinxhyphen{}based projection of the SAR satellite applied throughout this validation component.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
GOFS 3.1 Analysis runs at a \(1/12\)° global HYCOM resolution (\(\sim 9\) km at equator, \(\sim7\) km at mid\sphinxhyphen{}latitudes, \(\sim 3.5\) km at North Pole); ESPC\sphinxhyphen{}D\sphinxhyphen{}V02’s can run at a higher, \(1/25\)° (\(\sim\)3\textendash{}4 km at mid\sphinxhyphen{}latitudes), resolution (Barton et al. 2021). However, the version used by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} is regridded onto the same grid as GOFS 3.1. HYCOM consists of 3\sphinxhyphen{}hourly instantaneous analyses with 40 standard \(z\)\sphinxhyphen{}levels of which \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} selects the surface level (\(\texttt{depth}=0.0\)). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GLBy0.08/expt\_93.0}} publishes one combined \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{water\_u}}+\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{water\_v}} NetCDF/OPeNDAP dataset per calendar year; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ESPC\sphinxhyphen{}D\sphinxhyphen{}V02}} publishes one continuous OPeNDAP dataset per component spanning its whole coverage range.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data Quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
As a data\sphinxhyphen{}assimilative reanalysis/forecast product rather than a direct retrieval, HYCOM carries no per\sphinxhyphen{}cell observational quality flag. Instead its data quality depends on the underlying model, its initial state, and data assimilation checks. For ESPC\sphinxhyphen{}D\sphinxhyphen{}V02, all assimilated data go through a quality control system checking for gross error and assigning a likelihood of error based on comparison to ocean analyses (instrument error and representativeness error) (Barton et al. 2021).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
GOFS 3.1 Analysis (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{expt\_93.0}}): 04\sphinxhyphen{}12\sphinxhyphen{}2018 \sphinxhyphen{} 04\sphinxhyphen{}09\sphinxhyphen{}2024 (used by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} until 10\sphinxhyphen{}08\sphinxhyphen{}2024 12:00 UT). ESPC\sphinxhyphen{}D\sphinxhyphen{}V02: 10\sphinxhyphen{}08\sphinxhyphen{}2024 \sphinxhyphen{} present.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
HYCOM public THREDDS Data Server (\sphinxurl{https://tds.hycom.org/thredds/}), OPeNDAP endpoints \sphinxurl{https://tds.hycom.org/thredds/dodsC/ESPC-D-V02/u3z} (+\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{v3z}}) and \sphinxurl{https://tds.hycom.org/thredds/dodsC/GLBy0.08/expt\_93.0/uv3z/\{year\}}; openly accessible, no registration required. See also \sphinxurl{https://www.hycom.org/dataserver}.


\subsubsection{C\sphinxhyphen{}band SAR}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:c-band-sar-2}}\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:id7}}

\paragraph{Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}1 L2 OCN \sphinxhyphen{} RVL}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:sentinel-1-l2-ocn-rvl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The RVL (Radial Velocity) component of the Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}1 L2\_OCN product provides an estimate of the total Doppler frequency {[}Hz{]} and the corresponding radial LoS surface velocity {[}m/s{]}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rvlRadVel}}, obtained by fitting (least square minimization) the antenna model to the observed azimuth Doppler spectrum of the Level\sphinxhyphen{}1 SLC image. The estimated Doppler frequency is then corrected for antenna mis\sphinxhyphen{}pointing (as a function of elevation angle) and the attitude/orbit Doppler error (Engen and Johnsen 2011). Other relevant parameters in the RVL component include standard deviation, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rvlRadVelStd}}, and the acquisition geometry variables \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rvlHeading}} (along\sphinxhyphen{}track heading) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rvlIncidenceAngle}}. The RVL component is generated for all four Sentinel\sphinxhyphen{}1 imaging modes: WV, SM, IW, and EW (Engen and Johnsen 2011).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The spatial coverage of the RVL product equals that of the corresponding mode. In WV mode, RVL is thus computed on the same isolated \(\sim20\times20\) km vignette used by the rest of that mode’s OCN product, at roughly 200 km spacing along the orbit track. In SM/IW/EW mode, RVL is produced on a grid \(\sim 1 \times 1\) km similar to the OWI products. To compare an in\sphinxhyphen{}situ or model current vector (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EWCT}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NSCT}}) against this scalar radial measurement, the vector is projected onto the SAR line\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}sight in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} toolbox using
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}v_{\text{projection}} = \texttt{EWCT}\cdot\cos(\texttt{rvlHeading} - 90^{\circ}) + \texttt{NSCT}\cdot\sin(\texttt{rvlHeading} - 90^{\circ}),\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rvlHeading}} is stored in mathematical convention (counter\sphinxhyphen{}clockwise from East) and the \(-90^{\circ}\) term converts the along\sphinxhyphen{}track heading to the (right\sphinxhyphen{}looking) range direction.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Data Quality:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the RVL component, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rvlLandFlag}} is automatically set to 1 where a cell’s land coverage exceeds 10\% (Engen and Johnsen 2011). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} then masks both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rvlRadVel}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rvlRadVelStd}} as NaN’d at flagged cells. No separate per\sphinxhyphen{}cell QC\sphinxhyphen{}code flag exists for RVL beyond the land flag. Note that the operational \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rvlRadVel}} is known to carry substantial platform\sphinxhyphen{}induced biases, up to \(\sim\)2 m/s, from residual antenna mis\sphinxhyphen{}pointing and instrument effects (Martin et al. 2022). This is currently not compensated for in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{l2o\sphinxhyphen{}qc}} toolbox.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Availability:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
3 April 2014 \textendash{} present, across all four imaging modes (WV, SM, IW, EW).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dataset acquisition:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (\sphinxurl{https://dataspace.copernicus.eu/}); OData catalogue/download API at \sphinxurl{https://catalogue.dataspace.copernicus.eu/odata/v1/Products}; free registration required.


\subsubsection{HF radars}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:hf-radars}}

\paragraph{Copernicus Marine \sphinxhyphen{} global radar coverage}
\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:copernicus-marine-global-radar-coverage}}\label{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:subpar-hfr-cmems}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Description:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Gridded, total\sphinxhyphen{}vector surface\sphinxhyphen{}current field (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EWCT}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NSCT}}) from Copernicus Marine. Contributors are mainly European national HF\sphinxhyphen{}radar networks together with NOAA (further described in Section {\hyperref[\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:subpar-hfr-noaa}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{NOAA \sphinxhyphen{} US radar coverage}}}}}); every European region is processed through a single, centrally\sphinxhyphen{}coordinated pipeline, the EU HFR Node (Lorente et al. 2022). Additional variables are per\sphinxhyphen{}cell standard deviations \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EWCS}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NSCS}}, a geometric\sphinxhyphen{}dilution\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}precision field \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GDOP}}, and several QC flags including an overall \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{QCflag}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Characteristics:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
25 named regions, spanning the Mediterranean, Atlantic, North Sea, and Norwegian coasts (e.g. Galicia, Gibraltar, DeltaEbro, COSYNA, Skagerrak, Finnmark, Vestlandet) as well as the five US coastal areas also served by NOAA (Figures \hyperref[\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:fig-hf-radar-coverage-europe}]{Fig.\@ \ref{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:fig-hf-radar-coverage-europe}}} and \hyperref[\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:fig-hf-radar-coverage-us}]{Fig.\@ \ref{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:fig-hf-radar-coverage-us}}}), each operated by a different national institution (Table \hyperref[\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:tab-copernicus-hfr-resolutions}]{Table \ref{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:tab-copernicus-hfr-resolutions}}}) but converging on the same EU HFR Node distribution pipeline for the European regions. Near\sphinxhyphen{}real\sphinxhyphen{}time (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{latest\sphinxhyphen{}radar\sphinxhyphen{}total}}) coverage exists for 19 of the 25 regions; the remaining seven, ARPAS, COSYNA, Finnmark, US\sphinxhyphen{}Alaska, US\sphinxhyphen{}Hawaii, and WHub, are available only through the monthly/delayed\sphinxhyphen{}mode feed. Default layer\sphinxhyphen{}vs\sphinxhyphen{}layer collocation against the SAR grid is \(\pm\)30 min with a 6 km cell\sphinxhyphen{}averaging aggregation window and equal spatial weighting. This is adjustable through the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.yaml}} recipe file. Native grid resolution and cadence vary by region, where most regions contain hourly data. Exceptions are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{COSYNA}} (20 min) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NAdr}} (30 min). All available resolution are listed in Table \hyperref[\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:tab-copernicus-hfr-resolutions}]{Table \ref{\detokenize{05_reference_datasets:tab-copernicus-hfr-resolutions}}}.
